purpose: Freeze the claim-time xattr call, API, error, platform, ATP journey, marginal graph, and replacement-cost inventory; issue a terminal owner gate without authorizing implementation.

authority.decision_basis: The canonical ledger measures xattr as the only marginal package in every active Unix cell, so removing it does not remove rustix. The current integration has important proof and error-reporting gaps, but they are incumbent-hardening gaps. A replacement would add Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and NetBSD ABI, allocation-race, namespace, and unsafe-maintenance obligations without satisfying the stated rustix-parent trigger.

marginal_graph.interpretation: The ledger's baseline-minus-counterfactual package set is exactly xattr in every active cell. Because rustix is present in those baselines but absent from every marginal set, rustix remains after removing xattr in all measured profile, target, and host cells.

unsafe_cost.incumbent_boundary: xattr owns path/fd conversion, buffer initialization, Linux-like rustix calls, BSD libc calls, namespace conversion, and unsupported stubs; rustix owns the macOS position/options adaptation.
unsafe_cost.conclusion: A first-party replacement would widen Asupersync's reviewed unsafe and platform-maintenance surface while removing only the safe wrapper package and leaving rustix in every measured active cell.

decision.required_next_action: Route the thirteen gaps as incumbent integration, evidence, or documentation work. Close replacement children as not applicable under this gate; do not begin first-party design or implementation unless a reconsideration trigger produces a new owner-reviewed gate.
decision.rollback: No runtime source, manifest, lockfile, dependency, or registry artifact changed; retain xattr and this inventory as the claim-time baseline.

no_claim_boundaries: This source inventory does not prove macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, other-Unix, Windows, or wasm runtime behavior.
A target-filtered cargo metadata cell is dependency-graph evidence, not a runtime platform receipt.
The existing regular-file TCP fixture does not prove directory, symlink, permission, unsupported-filesystem, size-race, lifecycle, CLI, or other-transport behavior.
A test that returns when setup fails is not a typed unsupported-platform success claim.
Best-effort capture and apply do not prove complete metadata preservation or transactional rollback.
The marginal ledger does not prove runtime correctness, release readiness, or performance.
The ledger's root_native status remains unknown; marginal_native none does not certify the whole graph as native-code-free.
DEFER does not bless current integration gaps; it routes them without authorizing dependency replacement.
No local Cargo fallback or broad workspace-health claim is authorized by this focused inventory.
No file deletion, dependency removal, replacement child, or cutover is authorized.
